instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of jasmine rice under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Transfer it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Cover, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook for 12 minutes. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on until you serve.
Meanwhile, cut the chicken into 1 inch cubes and pat them dry. Mince the garlic.
In a large bowl, mix the chicken with the garlic, 1 1/2 tsp white pepper, 1 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 1/2 tbsp oyster sauce and 1 1/2 tbsp sugar. Leave it for 10 minutes.
While it sits, wash the lettuce and separate the leaves, and slice the cucumber. Arrange both on a platter.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until it shimmers.
Add half the chicken in a single layer. Leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and crisp at the edges.

Stir and cook for 3 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a piece there. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Transfer the chicken to a paper towel-lined plate. Cook the second half the same way.
Serve the chicken with the rice, lettuce and cucumber.
method_notes: The lead is Food.com's Mix Bowl Thai version, the only readable recipe under this exact name, and it has only 3 reviews, so this is a fallback lead. It marinates cubed chicken in garlic, white pepper, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar, then pan-fries it hot and serves it with lettuce and cucumber. The marinade is cut from 30 minutes to 10 and the peanut oil becomes a neutral oil to keep it nut-free. Taste Canada's garlic pepper chicken (a stir-fry with fried garlic) is a near dish and was only used to check the seasoning.
